name: Yaksha
_grid: One character per tile, row 0 = the far side (player 2), last row = player 1's side. Each character is defined in the legend. From the old map image (maps/yaksha.jpg): the 16x16 arena (columns 4-19), a cross of high ground round the big capture zone and a U of high ground before each team's spawns, water, trees, two side capture zones; and each player's 3x3 surprise box with its gifts. The boxes sit to the right of the arena, a gap away (player 2's top-left box would have landed on the table's top pillar: it's mirrored onto the right so its passages still face the arena).
_legend: level = height step (0 = lowest). surface picks the look from the palette. slant = slopes down to lower land over this many world units, inside the tile (0.559: a 60 degree slope). sink = the surface sits this many world units lower (a look only: the water counts as ground level). marker = something on the tile (painted, or a 3D piece with piece: true). zone: capture zone tiles (the big centre one, Z, a level above the terrace round it) (a frame per square group that takes the colour of the player with more Pokemon in it). tree / gift: a tree tile or a gift box, NOT locked (players move them). passage-inN: a secret passage's entrance in a surprise box; passage-outN: where passage N comes out (one way).
_board: The published board files the map picker uses (from tools/build_board.py; update when a new version is published), then run tools/build_arena_index.py.
_table: Image for the table around the board (placeholder until the arena gets its own).
_numbers: How the passage numbers read: "both" = a diagonal fraction N/N, upright top left, upside down bottom right, so either player reads it from their side (without it, numbers turn to face the nearer side edge).
_textures: Placeholders from tools/draw_placeholders.py, a shadowy temple garden at dusk (the user's OK): dark mossy slate ground (Chrysalia's), dark violet temple stone on the high ground, black-green water, the surprise boxes' floor with faint glowing violet runes, dark stone edges.
